---
title: "07 — Predict the separate 2025 year"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** how well models trained on 2014–2022 and calibrated on 2024 classify frequent mental distress in a *different year's respondents*. This notebook begins the independent-year evaluation.

Loads the saved classifiers selected using earlier data.
Applies the 2024-fitted calibrators without refitting them.
Scores 2025 respondents.
Calculates metrics only for respondents with valid FMD outcomes.
Preserves the model originally selected in 2023.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Score the untouched 2025 input file

Produces predictions for **every** 2025 record with valid survey weights, including
records with unknown FMD or unresolved race. Outcome filtering occurs only when
calculating supervised metrics.

```{r score-the-untouched-2025-input-file}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frozen-model scoring of 2025 records
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep valid-weight records even when their outcome or race group is unresolved.
# Apply previously saved models and calibrators without selecting a new classifier.

check_packages("data.table")
raw_test <- read_test_year()
all_test <- prepare_features(raw_test[valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)])
calibrators <- load_run_rds("models", "06_frozen_calibration")
selection <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")


# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (family in c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
    fitted <- load_run_rds("models", paste0("05_", family))
    raw_probability <- predict_classifier(fitted, all_test)
    frozen <- calibrators[[family]]
    adjusted <- calibrate_probabilities(
        raw_probability,
        frozen$intercept,
        frozen$slope
    )
    data.table::set(all_test, j = paste0("prob_", family), value = adjusted)
}

# Preserve original row identifiers for defensible joins and survey analyses.
selected_col <- paste0("prob_", selection$chosen_family)
all_test[, selected_probability := get(selected_col)]
keep <- c(
    "YEAR", "source_row_id", "STATE", "STRAT", "PSU", "RAW_WEIGHT",
    "FMD", "cohort", "AIAN_ALONE", feature_names,
    paste0("prob_", c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")),
    "selected_probability"
)
scored <- all_test[, ..keep]
if (anyDuplicated(scored$source_row_id)) {
    stop("2025 original row IDs are not unique")
}

# Persist this run-specific object for downstream stages without intentionally
# overwriting an existing artifact.
save_once_rds(scored, "checkpoints", "07_scored_2025")

response_audit <- scored[, .(
    respondents = .N,
    valid_outcomes = sum(valid_outcome(FMD)),
    unknown_outcomes = sum(!valid_outcome(FMD))
), by = cohort]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(response_audit, "07_2025_response_audit")
print(response_audit)
```


## Compare national 2025 performance

Evaluates survey-weighted AUROC, Brier score, and mean probability error in 2025 before
examining the AI/AN population separately. Includes the frozen training-prevalence-only
baseline.

```{r compare-national-2025-performance}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# National descriptive evaluation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Restrict supervised metrics to valid binary outcomes.
# Retain the 2023 selection flag; sorting 2025 errors does not redefine the winner.

eligible <- scored[valid_outcome(FMD)]
rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (family in c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
    rows[[family]] <- data.frame(
        family = family,
        weighted_metrics(
            eligible$FMD,
            eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]],
            eligible$RAW_WEIGHT
        )
    )
}
rows[["prevalence_only"]] <- data.frame(
    family = "prevalence_only",
    weighted_metrics(
        eligible$FMD,
        rep(selection$training_prevalence, nrow(eligible)),
        eligible$RAW_WEIGHT
    )
)
all_results <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)[order(brier)]
all_results[, chosen_in_2023 := family == selection$chosen_family]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(all_results, "07_2025_national_models")
print(all_results)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    all_results,
    ggplot2::aes(reorder(family, brier), brier, fill = family)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    atg_scale_fill_models() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "General-population model performance in 2025",
        subtitle = "Historical model selection was fixed before 2025 scoring",
        x = "Model",
        y = "Survey-weighted Brier score (lower is better)",
        fill = "Model family"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "07_2025_national_brier", 8, 5)
```


## Resampling intervals for national 2025 performance

Approximate 95% intervals for each model's AUROC, Brier score, and mean probability error, plus each model's Brier improvement over the prevalence-only baseline. Uses the same stratified PSU resampling as Notebook 12: whole PSUs are redrawn within the strata of the complete 2025 sample, the frozen predictions are held fixed, and every model is scored on the identical resample so differences between models keep their covariance.

These intervals reflect survey-sampling variation only. They do not include uncertainty from training, selecting, or calibrating the models. Strata with a single PSU are held fixed, which understates variance. They are exploratory percentile intervals, not CDC design-based inference.

```{r national-2025-intervals}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stratified PSU resampling of fixed 2025 predictions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (anyNA(scored[, .(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU, RAW_WEIGHT)])) {
    stop("Survey design identifiers cannot be missing for PSU resampling")
}
scored[, stratum_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, sep = "_")]
scored[, psu_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU, sep = "_")]

# Build strata from the complete weighted sample before restricting to valid FMD.
psu_table <- unique(scored[, .(stratum_key, psu_key)])
psu_table[, psu_index := seq_len(.N)]
strata_indices <- split(psu_table$psu_index, psu_table$stratum_key)
eligible <- scored[valid_outcome(FMD)]
eligible[, psu_index := psu_table$psu_index[match(psu_key, psu_table$psu_key)]]
if (anyNA(eligible$psu_index)) {
    stop("Could not map every observation to its original survey PSU")
}

model_probabilities <- c(
    stats::setNames(
        lapply(c("logistic", "lasso", "forest"), function(family) {
            eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
        }),
        c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")
    ),
    list(prevalence_only = rep(selection$training_prevalence, nrow(eligible)))
)

# Brier error, mean probability error, and AUROC for one set of weights.
interval_metrics <- function(weights) {
    rows <- lapply(names(model_probabilities), function(family) {
        probability <- model_probabilities[[family]]
        data.frame(
            family = family,
            auroc = if (family == "prevalence_only") {
                0.5
            } else {
                weighted_auc(eligible$FMD, probability, weights)
            },
            brier = weighted_mean((probability - eligible$FMD)^2, weights),
            mean_error = weighted_mean(probability - eligible$FMD, weights)
        )
    })
    result <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)
    baseline_brier <- result[family == "prevalence_only", brier]
    result[, brier_improvement := baseline_brier - brier]
    result
}

point_estimates <- interval_metrics(eligible$RAW_WEIGHT)

set.seed(seed + 707L)
replicate_list <- vector("list", psu_bootstrap_replicates)
for (replicate in seq_len(psu_bootstrap_replicates)) {
    counts <- integer(nrow(psu_table))
    for (indices in strata_indices) {
        if (length(indices) == 1L) {
            # A single PSU cannot be resampled; keep it fixed.
            counts[indices] <- 1L
        } else {
            draws <- sample.int(length(indices), size = length(indices), replace = TRUE)
            counts[indices] <- tabulate(draws, nbins = length(indices))
        }
    }
    resampled <- interval_metrics(eligible$RAW_WEIGHT * counts[eligible$psu_index])
    resampled[, replicate := replicate]
    replicate_list[[replicate]] <- resampled
    if (replicate %% 25L == 0L) {
        cat("[BOOTSTRAP] Finished", replicate, "PSU replicates\n")
    }
}
replicates_2025 <- data.table::rbindlist(replicate_list)
save_table(replicates_2025, "07_2025_national_psu_replicates")

metric_columns <- c("auroc", "brier", "mean_error", "brier_improvement")
interval_table <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(metric_columns, function(metric) {
    data.table::rbindlist(lapply(names(model_probabilities), function(family_name) {
        values <- replicates_2025[family == family_name][[metric]]
        values <- values[is.finite(values)]
        # Constant quantities (e.g. the baseline's AUROC) have no sampling spread.
        data.table::data.table(
            family = family_name,
            metric = metric,
            point_estimate = point_estimates[family == family_name][[metric]],
            ci_lower = if (length(values) >= 30L) stats::quantile(values, 0.025, names = FALSE) else NA_real_,
            ci_upper = if (length(values) >= 30L) stats::quantile(values, 0.975, names = FALSE) else NA_real_,
            valid_replicates = length(values)
        )
    }))
}))
save_table(interval_table, "07_2025_national_intervals")
print(interval_table)
```


## Visualize national 2025 intervals

```{r show-national-2025-intervals}
# Prevalence-only has no AUROC spread; drop its constant rows and the zero baseline gain.
plot_intervals <- interval_table[
    !(family == "prevalence_only" & metric %in% c("auroc", "brier_improvement"))
]
plot_intervals[, metric_label := factor(
    metric,
    levels = c("auroc", "brier", "brier_improvement", "mean_error"),
    labels = c("AUROC", "Brier score", "Brier improvement over baseline",
               "Mean predicted minus observed")
)]
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_intervals,
    ggplot2::aes(x = point_estimate, y = family, color = family)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper)) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric_label, scales = "free_x") +
    atg_scale_color_models() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "National 2025 performance with approximate 95% intervals",
        subtitle = "Stratified PSU resampling of fixed predictions; sampling variation only",
        x = NULL,
        y = NULL
    )
show_and_save(plot, "07_2025_national_intervals", 10, 6)
```
